contracts.boundary: Every configuration source layer and the merged effective policy are structurally validated against the shipped schema.json on load, reload, boot, and prospective apply. Findings name the offending path, and only a finding that makes a source unusable rejects the layer.
contracts.assertions: Unknown fields, invalid enum values, and wrong types produce config.schema_unsupported_field, config.schema_enum, and config.schema_type diagnostics at the exact path. A partial layer may defer schemaVersion conditionals that the effective configuration enforces. A schema copy that adds a field accepts what the installed schema still rejects, so acceptance follows schema.json instead of duplicated code. categoryStrategies keeps its strategy enum for every key, so a per-tier typo still produces a finding while the version 3 metadata key accepts free text. The offline validation report and its JSON form carry the same structural findings as warnings with the offending path.

boundaryTest.name: rejects unsupported fields, invalid values, and wrong types in source layers

invariant.name: validates partial layers without in-document version requirements and enforces them on the effective config

fault.name: makes schema edits, not code edits, decide what is accepted

contracts.boundary: Inline description metadata is valid in fixed-shape sections under every supported schema version and inside dynamically keyed maps under schemaVersion 3. It is preserved in the authored file and stripped before routing.
contracts.assertions: A loaded configuration contains no description key or text. Described and undescribed configurations load to identical routing policy. A version 2 tier named description keeps its pools. An ambiguous version 3 upgrade fails closed with a diagnostic naming models.description. A version 3 layer that puts a non-string value on a reserved key is rejected instead of being stripped, so routing never continues with the key silently deleted. Admission rule IDs one level below economics.tierOverrides keep their meaning in every version and reach routing unchanged.

boundaryTest.name: accepts inline descriptions in every supported section and strips them at the load boundary

invariant.name: does not change effective routing when descriptions are added or removed

fault.name: keeps a user-defined description key meaning under versions 1 and 2

contracts.boundary: Boot, reload, init, and background setup report the structural findings the domain validators own without stopping routing. An unusable source still blocks generation, init, and reconciliation writes.
contracts.assertions: Boot prints one [bifrost/config] warning line per structural finding and keeps routing. Reload logs the warnings after installing the configuration. A prospective init write stays blocked by unusable diagnostics. Generated bootstrap configuration carries only supported schema versions and no unsupported classifier field.

boundaryTest.name: blocks generation when a higher supported schema masks an unsupported lower layer

invariant.name: merges description-bearing layers and reports structural layer findings

fault.name: blocks generation when a project config source is malformed

contracts.boundary: Explicit tier fallback policies apply under every schema version that supports them (2 and 3) and stay inert under version 1, without changing candidate resolution.
contracts.assertions: A version 3 configuration resolves its declared fallback tier exactly like version 2. The semantic validators keep rejecting unsupported versions, unknown tiers, self-links, and cycles.

boundaryTest.name: keeps every version 2 routing capability under schemaVersion 3

invariant.name: requires version 2 for tierPolicies and rejects unsupported versions

fault.name: validates fallback tier references, duplicates, self-links, cycles, and namespace fields

contracts.boundary: Every isolated Pi extension copy used by the native and live acceptance harnesses now carries schema.json next to the TypeScript sources, and the replay guard baseline tracks the current index.ts region.
contracts.assertions: Real AgentSession abort, manual, false, and throw cases still pass with the copied schema. The real v1 output-effect and tool-effect guard faults still reach their named no-replay assertions and restore GREEN on the exact new index hash.

boundaryTest.name: cancels real AgentSession activation behind a proven deny-all fence

invariant.name: anchors the baseline source hash and proves isSideEffectFreeAllowanceFailure faults the output-effect no-replay assertion

fault.name: proves autoBoundaryStillActive faults the synthetic tool side-effect no-replay assertion

contracts.boundary: The resolve-only API now depends on ajv at runtime, so the packed consumer installs the runtime dependency closure offline instead of symlinking only host-provided dev dependencies.
contracts.assertions: A clean consumer installs no Pi packages, compiles the complete strict declaration graph, and runs both examples. A Pi import injected into the installed router graph still fails the named dependency assertion and restores GREEN.

boundaryTest.name: compiles and runs the shipped examples in a clean standalone consumer with no Pi packages installed

invariant.name: installs the packed JS API and resolves without loader flags on Node 22.19+

fault.name: rejects a Pi dependency injected into the actual packed router graph and restores it

contracts.boundary: The bifrost_config agent tool inspects Pi's real catalog and every config layer, checks a candidate offline, previews bounded route decisions without dispatching, and applies one approved config file atomically through the same reload path as /bifrost reload.
contracts.assertions: check and preview never write or dispatch; apply writes only after an answered approval, rejects changed candidate bytes, changed selected source, changed layers, changed model inventory, and unsafe sources; the previous config survives a failed write; a saved-but-not-activated write is reported honestly; unknown operations fail closed; config-layer paths come from the shared merge-order helper.

boundaryTest.name: checks, applies through an answered approval, saves one source, and activates it

invariant.name: compares the effective policy before and after without writing

fault.name: rejects a proposal whose candidate bytes changed

contracts.boundary: The skills/configure-bifrost skill and the bifrost_config tool ship inside the pi package and register alongside the extension, with bundled references resolving from the skill directory.
contracts.assertions: The packed archive contains the skill directory and the extension registration; the skill frontmatter parses, the always-loaded description stays short, bundled references resolve, and the skill names the tool and its safety gates.

boundaryTest.name: is included in the published package

invariant.name: registers the agent tool alongside the extension

fault.exception: Packaging is evidence-shaped by construction: the packed-archive inclusion assertion fails directly when a file is missing from the package file list, so there is no separate production fault to inject.

contracts.boundary: The reviewed production baseline sha256 recorded once in tests/fixtures/replay-fault-control.mjs and repeated in six integration fault gates must equal the reviewed committed index.ts, so offline fault proofs copy, mutate, and restore the real source.
contracts.assertions: Each named fault control starts GREEN on the pristine copy, turns its named assertion RED under the controlled production mutation, restores the source, and records restored GREEN; the baseline constant equals the reviewed index.ts sha256 so no gate refuses the proof.

boundaryTest.name: fault control: leaking the prompt projection turns the named redaction assertion RED

invariant.name: fault control: removing the late-abort guard allows forbidden late dispatch

fault.name: fails the named hard-exclusion assertion under a hard-filter-bypass fault in an isolated copy

contracts.boundary: Release and usage documentation for the goal-driven configuration tool, its skill, and the updated coverage map.
contracts.assertions: The changelog entry, README goal-first usage section, and the R07 coverage row describe the shipped tool, skill, and safety gates accurately; the description stays consistent with the implemented tool contract.

boundaryTest.exception: Documentation-only change with no runtime behavior to execute; accuracy is review-verified against the tool contract tests above.

invariant.exception: Documentation-only change with no runtime behavior to execute; accuracy is review-verified against the tool contract tests above.

fault.exception: Documentation-only change with no runtime behavior to execute; there is no production fault to inject.

contracts.boundary: The release-gates job carries a hard job-level timeout that fits the whole four-stage release sequence (acceptance, CRAP trend refresh, proposed-merge acceptance, report uploads) on the slowest hosted runners; a 45-minute budget killed a fully green run mid-stage.
contracts.assertions: The workflow suite proves release-gates declares timeout-minutes between 60 and 360 minutes, and a controlled rewrite to 45 minutes turns that named budget assertion red while the seven-gate job contract stays intact.

boundaryTest.name: release-gates keeps a hard budget that fits every release stage

invariant.name: release-gates stays unconditional with all seven gates and the report publishers

fault.name: fault control: a 45-minute release-gates budget turns the named budget assertion red
